speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Max Hodak.
zh: 我叫 Max Hodak。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm the CEO of a company called Science.
zh: 我是一家名为 Science 的公司的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk a little bit about infrastructure at startups.
zh: 我们要聊一点关于初创公司基础设施的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've spent most of my life working on brain-computer interfaces.
zh: 我人生的大部分时间都在做脑机接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is almost 20 years ago now.
zh: 那几乎是 20 年前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started my career as an undergrad working in a lab at Duke.
zh: 我以本科生的身份在杜克大学的一个实验室里开始了我的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is from our very first Society for Neuroscience conference.
zh: 这是我们第一次参加神经科学学会会议时的照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: The experiment I was working on back then was if you put electrodes in the brain of a monkey and then give a monkey a joystick and you record the neural activity as it's playing a game, if you make the joystick, say, the cursor go sideways when they push forward on the joystick, which does the brain do?
zh: 我当时在做的实验是：如果你把电极植入猴子的大脑，然后给猴子一个操纵杆，并在它玩游戏时记录神经活动——如果你让操纵杆，比如说，在他们向前推操纵杆时光标向侧面移动，大脑会怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the brain represent the joystick or the screen or something else?
zh: 大脑表征的是操纵杆，还是屏幕，还是别的什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out that there are neurons that do both.
zh: 结果发现，两种表征的神经元都存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: At our company, Science, our main product is a retinal prosthesis.
zh: 在我们的公司 Science，我们的主要产品是一种视网膜假体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a chip that's implanted under the retina in the back of the eye to restore vision to patients that have gone blind due to loss of the rods and cones in their eye.
zh: 它是一片植入眼睛后部视网膜下方的芯片，用于为因眼中视杆细胞和视锥细胞丧失而失明的患者恢复视力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although this is one of our patients on the cover of Time last November.
zh: 去年 11 月，我们的一位患者登上了《时代》杂志的封面。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the right, you can see there's a picture of the implant with the glasses.
zh: 在右边，你可以看到一张带有眼镜的植入体照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: So every little one of those hex grids that you see on the implant is essentially a solar cell.
zh: 你在植入体上看到的每一个小六边形网格，本质上都是一个太阳能电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when this is implanted under the retina, the patient wears glasses that have a camera that sees the world and a laser projector that projects onto the implant.
zh: 当它植入视网膜下方后，患者佩戴的眼镜上有一个观察世界的摄像头和一个投影到植入体上的激光投影仪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it projects the image in infrared, wherever the light is absorbed on the implant, it creates a little electric field to excite the retina, thereby directly bypassing the dead rods and cones to stimulate.
zh: 当它以红外线投影图像时，植入体上 wherever 光被吸收的地方就会产生一个微小的电场来刺激视网膜，从而直接绕过坏死的视杆细胞和视锥细胞进行刺激。

speaker: Unknown
en: This visual signal back into the retina, the first possible opportunity.
zh: 把这个视觉信号在第一个可能的时机重新送回视网膜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a pretty cool product.
zh: 这是一个相当酷的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It finished major clinical trials last year.
zh: 它去年完成了主要临床试验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been in three clinical trials now.
zh: 它现在已经历了三次临床试验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was covered in the BBC last fall.
zh: 去年秋天 BBC 报道过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of our patients finished a 300-page novel with the device and mailed us the book.
zh: 我们的一位患者用这个设备读完了一本 300 页的小说，并把书寄给了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm not going to talk about this work for the most part for the next 30 minutes.
zh: 但在接下来的 30 分钟里，我大部分时间不会讲这项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk about infrastructure and lessons.
zh: 我们要讲的是基础设施和经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is startup school.
zh: 毕竟，这是 Startup School。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's some things that you'll find useful in your company.
zh: 也许其中有些东西会对你的公司有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Picasso was noted for saying that when art critics get together they talk about form and structure and meaning and when artists get together they talk about where to buy cheap turpentine.
zh: 毕加索有句名言：艺术评论家聚在一起时，谈论的是形式、结构和意义；而艺术家聚在一起时，谈论的是去哪里买便宜的松节油。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is also often phrased as amateurs talk strategy professionals talk logistics.
zh: 这句话也常被表述为：业余者谈战略，专业人士谈后勤。

speaker: Unknown
en: A quote from a guy that the United States named a tank after.
zh: 这是引自一位美国以他命名了坦克的人的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are surprisingly few lessons that are really broad across companies.
zh: 而令人惊讶的是，真正能横跨各公司的普适经验其实很少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, the experience of running a startup is you're just looking at kind of a continual stream of facts that hit your desk every day, and you're trying to make the best local decision that you can for those facts.
zh: 通常，经营初创公司的体验是：你每天面对的是不断涌到你桌面上的一系列事实，而你只是在努力针对这些事实做出你能做出的最佳局部决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it looks inconsistent over weeks, that's usually the way to go.
zh: 而且如果这些决策在几周内看起来前后不一致，那通常就是正确的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are a couple topics that keep...
zh: 但有几个话题会不断……

speaker: Unknown
en: kind of very repeatedly coming up that are kind of universal experiences, at least for deep tech companies, which is the thing that I kind of know most of my experiences in, not just pure software.
zh: 反复地出现，它们算得上是普遍经验，至少对深科技公司而言是这样——这是我最熟悉的大多数经验所在的领域，而不仅仅是纯软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are things that keep coming up, like buying things.
zh: 所以有些东西会不断出现，比如买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your first reaction might be that if you do software, you don't need to buy things.
zh: 你的第一反应可能是：如果你做软件，你不需要买任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be me alone in an empty room with some computers, writing software, and this is going to be how we build a company.
zh: 会是我独自一人在一个空房间里，对着几台电脑写软件，我们就这样把公司建起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if this is you, yes, you have figured out a reason why VCs love funding software and why they've done so much of it for the last 25 years.
zh: 如果你是这么想的，没错，你已经想明白了为什么风投热爱投资软件、为什么过去 25 年他们投了这么多软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you do anything other than pure software, you'll be buying many, many thousands of things.
zh: 但只要你做的不是纯软件，你就会买到成千上万种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is us.
zh: 这是我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: About, I think, six months into the company.
zh: 大概是公司成立六个月的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a little tough to make out.
zh: 虽然有点看不太清。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a lot of computers.
zh: 这里有很多电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also a bunch of microscopes and other electronics and 3D printers and resin and PCBs.
zh: 还有一堆显微镜、其他电子设备、3D 打印机、树脂和 PCB。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're buying things really continuously.
zh: 你真的是在持续不断地买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it might sound really obvious, like a really basic question, like you surely just buy things.
zh: 所以这听起来可能非常显而易见，像一个非常基础的问题，比如你肯定就是直接买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for you as the founder, you can use a credit card.
zh: 对你作为创始人来说，你可以用信用卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Credit cards work great.
zh: 信用卡非常好用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can buy lots of things with credit cards.
zh: 你可以用信用卡买很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also send a wire transfer.
zh: 你也可以电汇。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is, how does your 17th employee buy things?
zh: 问题是,你的第 17 名员工怎么买东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they have a credit card?
zh: 他们有信用卡吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say you hand out credit cards to all of your employees and tell them to buy what they need.
zh: 假设你给所有员工都发了信用卡，告诉他们需要什么就买什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you start getting messages like this.
zh: 于是你开始收到这样的消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you think like, you know, I care about burn.
zh: 然后你想，你知道，我在乎 burn。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to spend efficiently.
zh: 我们必须高效地花钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to approve all of the purchases as they happen.
zh: 我要逐笔审批所有采购。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you get a message like this, and then you think $3,000 sounds like a lot for a power supply.
zh: 真正的问题是归因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we need a $3,000 power supply?
zh: 我们需要 3000 美元的电源吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What if we get one from an auction?
zh: 要是我们从拍卖会上买一个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in three days, there's an auction.
zh: 比如三天后就有一场拍卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we'll get it for half off.
zh: 也许我们能半价拿下。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can get it in two weeks.
zh: 我们可以两周后拿到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you also remember that you've hired some very highly paid and talented employees.
zh: 但你也想起，你雇了一些薪水很高、非常有才华的员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And are you saying they can't get the tools that they need?
zh: 你是在说他们拿不到所需的工具吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That you're spending $100,000 a week.
zh: 你每周可是要花 10 万美元的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you wait a week to get a power supply half off, you have certainly dwarfed any possible benefit from getting it.
zh: 如果你为半价等一周才拿到电源，你肯定已经把可能省下的好处远远抵消掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, and if they were Anthropic, they're not gonna be hassled over a $3,000 purchase.
zh: 而且，你知道，如果他们是 Anthropic,他们不会为了一笔 3000 美元的采购被刁难。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just gonna have a power supply.
zh: 他们就是直接有个电源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you realize is not only is this very hard to keep Burn under control,
zh: 于是你意识到，不仅很难控制 burn,

speaker: Unknown
en: But also, it's just this is the inappropriate place to exercise spending review.
zh: 而且，这根本就不是行使支出审查的合适场合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spending review has to come earlier.
zh: 支出审查必须更早进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to have some concept of budgeting.
zh: 你必须有一些预算的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not really about even just the payment rail of buying a thing.
zh: 这其实甚至不仅仅是买东西的支付通道问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how do you understand the bucket of money that you have?
zh: 而是你如何理解你手里那一桶钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't want to be making the $1,500 power supply versus $3,000 power supply trade-off.
zh: 我不想去做 1500 美元电源还是 3000 美元电源这种取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: They need to understand the resources that they have so that they can make trade-offs within those real resources.
zh: 他们需要理解自己拥有的资源，这样才能在这些真实资源之内做出取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you set up a procurement system.
zh: 于是你建立了一个采购系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now your highly paid employees are spending their days clicking around B2B enterprise SaaS.
zh: 现在你那些高薪员工整天都在点来点去地折腾 B2B 企业级 SaaS。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out that from the time that they place an order for a power supply, it takes two weeks to arrive because you can't actually buy that with a credit card.
zh: 结果发现，从他们下单买电源开始，要两周才能到货，因为你根本没法用信用卡买这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to set up an account with the vendor and deal with insurance and certification paperwork and get an account set up.
zh: 你必须和供应商建立账户，处理保险和认证文书，把账户开起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have to generate a quote so that you can generate a purchase order so that you can generate an invoice.
zh: 他们必须先生成报价单，这样你才能生成采购订单，这样你才能生成发票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now everyone's upset that things are taking super long to get ordered.
zh: 现在所有人都因为下单要花超长时间而不满。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this actually really requires like a, like this is a living organism.
zh: 所以这实际上真的需要，比如，这是一个活的有机体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when people move from academia to startups, I think one of the reactions that people often have is like, why are there people whose job there is to purchase things?
zh: 当人们从学术界转到创业公司时，我想人们常常会有一种反应，就是：为什么那里有些人的工作就是采购东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Surely I can just buy things.
zh: 我肯定自己就能买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But absolutely there are people whose job is to buy things.
zh: 但确实有人专门负责买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the time that you submit the order, going back and forth with the vendor to set all of this up is very time consuming and it can easily stretch out.
zh: 从你提交订单开始，和供应商来回沟通把这一切都建起来是非常耗时的，而且很容易拖长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes like active management to metrics.
zh: 这需要主动的管理、要盯指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: To cause these things to go fast.
zh: 才能让这些事情快速推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think part of what, like when we think about this, we have a reputation I think of often being very quick and people are unsure like how does that happen?
zh: 我觉得，当我们思考这个问题时，我想我们常常有一个以非常快速著称的名声，人们不确定这是怎么做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It is mostly not that we are smarter, it is infrastructure like this, that is the, like how speed is built.
zh: 这主要不是因为我们更聪明，而是这样的基础设施，速度就是这样建立起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now people can buy things.
zh: 所以现在人们可以买东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least you can keep overall burn under control.
zh: 至少你能控制总体 burn 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you know that you're not going to exceed some large amount of spending every month.
zh: 现在你知道你每个月不会超过某个大额支出了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you realize that that wasn't really the problem.
zh: 然后你意识到，那其实并不是真正的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could figure out your runway.
zh: 你可以算出自己的 runway。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is attribution.
zh: 问题在于归因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is when you're doing, whether you're working on rockets or cars or drugs or brain-computer interfaces or anything that involves dealing with the real world, you realize that one of your other problems is that you're buying stuff in bulk.
zh: 就是在你做，无论你是在做火箭、汽车、药物、脑机接口，还是任何涉及与现实世界打交道的事情，你意识到你的另一个问题是你在大批量采购东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we buy gases from argon to silane to nitrogen to resins to media.
zh: 比如我们购买各种气体，从氩气到硅烷到氮气，还有树脂和培养基。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we buy these things in bulk and we part them out to lots of different experiments.
zh: 然后我们批量购买这些东西，再把它们分配到很多不同的实验中去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, when you do this, attribution is pretty difficult.
zh: 现在，当你这样做时，成本归因是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if nobody knows how much an experiment costs, like every time you grow up a new cell line or every time we make a new probe in the fab, how much does that loop cost?
zh: 所以如果没人知道一个实验要花多少钱，比如每次培养一个新的细胞系，或者每次我们在 fab 里做一个新的探针，这个循环要花多少钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody knows.
zh: 没有人知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Therefore, experiments are free.
zh: 因此，实验是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't cost dollars.
zh: 你觉得自己需要四年时间，需要 20 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It costs media, and media comes from the fridge.
zh: 它花的是培养基，而培养基来自冰箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to know how do we price a thing that we make.
zh: 而我们想知道的是，如何为我们制造的东西定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: We make a bunch of things in volume in the Foundry.
zh: 我们在 Foundry 里批量制造很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to know what can we sell that for.
zh: 我们想知道能卖多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That requires all of these spreadsheets to get an estimate of the pricing.
zh: 这需要所有这些电子表格来得到一个定价估算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's opinions in here.
zh: 而这里面有主观意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are not all facts.
zh: 这些并不全是事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much do you include rent?
zh: 房租要算进去多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much do you include depreciation of the tools?
zh: 设备的折旧要算进去多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: This comes with opinions about your future volume.
zh: 这还伴随着关于你未来产量的主观意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this is required to understand not just what you should charge, but also what you're spending and what your runway is.
zh: 所有这些都是必需的，不仅要理解你应该收多少钱，还要理解你在花多少钱、你的 runway 是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to deal with this, we've built...
zh: 为了解决这个问题，我们构建了……

speaker: Unknown
en: A huge amount of internal software at the company for managing this.
zh: 公司内部大量的软件来管理这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the first things that we did is almost everything that you can do in the company is a button somewhere in the software.
zh: 我们最早做的事情之一，就是公司里几乎所有你能做的事，都是软件里某处的一个按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it Helix, including stuff like purchasing.
zh: 我们叫它 Helix，包括采购之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because this extends all the way through to manufacturing, where we have every step that happens in the lab in the database, we can correlate all of this through and get this information.
zh: 而且因为这一直延伸到制造环节，实验室里发生的每一步都在数据库里，我们就可以把所有这些关联起来，得到这些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these like, again, so it turns out that for every iteration of a wafer that we make, in this case, for this protocol, it costs $40,000.
zh: 再说一次，结果发现，对于我们制造的每一轮晶圆迭代，在这个例子里，对于这个协议，要花费 4 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like a lot of money.
zh: 这是一大笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you might have raised, let's say you raised $20 million in a Series A.
zh: 你可能融了，比如说你在 Series A 融了 2000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: You think you need four years, you need 20 people.
zh: 你以为你需要四年,需要 20 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my experience, about half the burn is headcount.
zh: 按我的经验，大约一半的 burn 是人力成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say 20 people, that's probably three, three and a half, that's like three million a year in revenue.
zh: 所以比如说 20 个人，那大概是三年，三年半，那大概是每年 300 万美元的支出。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's half of your burn.
zh: 那是你 burn 的一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need 20,000 square feet, about $4 a square foot.
zh: 你需要 2 万平方英尺，大约每平方英尺 4 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's another 750,000 to a million a year.
zh: 那又是一年 75 万到 100 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now suddenly you've got really, it's a $3 million a year research budget for three or four years.
zh: 所以突然间，你实际上拥有的是一个每年 300 万美元、持续三四年的研究预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: That goes way faster than you think.
zh: 这笔钱花得比你想象的快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, your team just saw that you raised a larger amount of money than they've ever seen in their lives.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

en: This is a heavily redacted version of the internal interface, but hopefully you can make out the idea of what's going on here.

zh: 这样我们可以把这个初始审阅的投票分散到公司的很多人身上，这一点至关重要，因为如果你做的事情很酷，等你做到几年之后，漏斗顶端会泛滥成灾。

zh: 但即便如此，你仍然需要一些方法来对团队其他成员的判断做平均。

zh: 而投票机制通常是一种非常好的方式。

zh: 这些是我们过去几年的实际统计数据。

zh: 我们收到的漏斗顶端申请中有 17% 进入电话初筛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, that first initial app voting stage is drawn from a company-wide pool so that we can get the voting done quickly within usually 24 or 48 hours and not bottleneck that on any small group of people.
zh: 再说一次，那个最初的申请投票阶段是从全公司的池子里抽人的，这样我们通常能在 24 或 48 小时内快速完成投票，而不会让这件事成为任何一小群人的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: The phone screen is again drawn from a company-wide pool of people.
zh: 电话初筛同样是从全公司的池子里抽人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not team-specific.
zh: 这不是按团队划分的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你是否达到了技术能力和展示出的学习能力的基本门槛？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你的生活看起来像不像你曾经有过的那些抱负？

speaker: Unknown
en: And do you have specific ambitions for your life?
zh: 你对你的人生是否有具体的抱负？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this we can distribute over the entire company.
zh: 所以这一步我们可以分散到整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then half of those tend to go to homework.
zh: 然后其中一半通常会进入作业环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, we'd be using entirely AI-resistant homeworks now.
zh: 理想情况下，我们现在会使用完全抗 AI 的作业。

zh: 所以我们最喜欢的作业类型是那些不会饱和、天花板很高，并且天然可以打分成两三个可以画在图上的数字的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that when we get responses to homework, we can just plot them all.
zh: 这样当我们收到作业的答卷时，就可以直接把它们全部画在图上。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: In cases where that's not possible for homework right now, we're doing increasing number of technical phone calls or onsite practical tests, but ideally we would have an AI-resistant take-home for each of these.
zh: 在目前作业无法做到这一点的情况下，我们正在增加技术电话面试或现场实操测试的数量，但理想情况下，我们希望每一步都有一个抗 AI 的带回家作业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic had a really interesting take on the AI-resistant homework where they've had a couple tasks where there's like, it's like the GPU kernel optimization, like what is the minimum number of cycles you can get it down to, and this is naturally adjusting, like the hurdle for a while was, I think it was Sonnet's performance, and if you could beat that, then you could get an interview.
zh: Anthropic 对抗 AI 的作业有一个非常有趣的思路，他们有过几个任务，比如 GPU kernel 优化，比如你能把周期数压到最少多少，这是天然可以调整的，比如有一段时间门槛是，我记得是 Sonnet 的性能，如果你能超过它，你就能拿到面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there's a bunch of ways to construct AI resistance and homeworks.
zh: 我认为有很多种方法可以构造抗 AI 的作业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then by the time you get to the interview, it is important that you have from there reasonably high, like at least 25% conversion to an offer, because otherwise it is just, you're gonna waste too much of your time doing onsites for employees that don't convert.
zh: 然后等你到了面试环节，重要的是从这里开始要有合理偏高的转化率，比如至少 25% 转化为 offer，否则的话，你会浪费太多时间在那些不会转化的员工身上做 onsite。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't get that down.
zh: 你不能把这个比例降下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's four steps to this.
zh: 所以这里有四个步骤。

en: Initial voting, the phone screen, homework, and a full interview.

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is, as far as from my experience, this is the minimum set of information that we need to make a full decision.
zh: 而就我的经验而言，这是我们要做出完整决定所需的最少信息集。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think that there's a more efficient way to elicit this.
zh: 而且我不认为有比这更高效的方式来引出这些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there's a smaller number of steps that we could use.
zh: 我不认为我们可以用更少的步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this has become our process.

en: So you're hiring people, they're coming into work, they're starting, they're incurring payroll, but how do you know that you're good at this?
zh: 那么你在招人，他们来上班了，他们开始了，他们在产生工资开销，但你怎么知道自己在这方面做得好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like eventually you'll get feedback from the market on how good you are at hiring because the company will work or it won't.
zh: 你最终会从市场上得到关于你招聘水平如何的反馈，因为公司要么成功要么失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like your team will be capable of accomplishing the stuff that you've set out and they'll help you course correct through that.
zh: 你的团队会能够完成你设定的那些事情，他们会帮助你在这个过程中纠正方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is a very, very long feedback and it's a very poorly behaved loss function.
zh: 但这是一个非常、非常长的反馈，而且是一个表现非常糟糕的损失函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's kind of your job as management to design synthetic gradients that allow you to find out earlier and along the way how recruiting is going and if you need a course correction.
zh: 所以作为管理者，你的职责之一就是设计合成梯度，让你能够更早地、在过程中就了解招聘进展如何，以及是否需要纠正方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: A conventional answer to this is the 360 review process.
zh: 对此一个常规的答案是 360 评估流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once a year, you send out a lot of forums, you gather up a bunch of feedback around each employee, you set up a bunch of meetings with HR and with the various managers, and you can do the conventional performance review cycle, which...
zh: 每年一次，你发出大量表单，围绕每位员工收集一堆反馈，你安排一堆和 HR 以及各位经理的会议，然后你可以做传统的绩效评估周期，它……

speaker: Unknown
en: Based on my experiences, this is a very disruptive process that doesn't tend to surface issues that you don't already know about but haven't acted on because you knew that thing was there, but firing people is hard, and so people drag their feet on it, and this is kind of reinforcing things you already knew.
zh: 根据我的经验，这是一个非常具有破坏性的流程，它往往不会浮现出那些你还不知道的问题，它只会强化你已经知道但尚未采取行动的事情，因为你知道那个问题存在，但是开除人很难，所以人们会拖延，这基本上就是在强化你已经知道的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it only happens once a year, maybe twice a year if you split up the company into cohorts.
zh: 而且它一年只发生一次，如果你把公司分成几个批次，也许一年两次。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think really what would be nice to have is a signal that...
zh: 但我认为真正理想的是拥有一个信号，它……

speaker: Unknown
en: Gives you this kind of natural feedback from across the company about who's good and who isn't and what's working and what's not in a way that is largely unbiased and is more continuous.
zh: 以一种基本无偏的、更加连续的方式，给你来自全公司范围的自然反馈，关于谁优秀、谁不优秀、什么在起作用、什么没有起作用。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 想象一下，如果你能每隔几周就得到关于哪里有问题、哪里进展顺利的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the process that I had developed, which I've now used for the last six or seven years, is every...
zh: 所以我开发出的这个流程，我已经用了六七年了，是每……

speaker: Unknown
en: Every couple weeks, every four to six weeks, it's not that often.
zh: 每隔几周，每四到六周一次，并不那么频繁。

speaker: Unknown
en: People around the company get pinged with a question through the software, through Helix.
zh: 公司里的人们会通过软件，通过 Helix，被一个问题 ping 到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a form, but there's only one question that really matters, which is knowing how this person turned out, would you vote again today for their hire?
zh: 有一个表单，但只有一个真正重要的问题，那就是：在知道这个人的表现之后，你今天还会再次为他们的录用投票吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same questions we use on the initial voting.
zh: 这和我们在初步投票中使用的是同一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you'll get a prompt to say, like, this person you work with, like, how would you vote for their hire today?
zh: 然后你会收到一个提示，比如，这位和你共事的人，你今天会为他们录用投什么票？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what we can do is we construct a graph over the company of all of the feedback.
zh: 然后我们要做的是，基于所有这些反馈在公司范围内构建一个图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the basic intuition is that your vote should be weighted more highly if everybody else has rated you highly.
zh: 基本直觉是：如果其他所有人都给你打了高分，你的投票权重就应该更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the astute may notice that this looks a lot like the original Google algorithm, PageRank, which is an idea called eigenvector centrality, where you can create a weight over the graph by looking at how the graph points together.
zh: 敏锐的人可能会注意到，这看起来很像 Google 最初的算法 PageRank，它是一个叫特征向量中心性的想法，你可以通过观察图中各点如何相互指向来创建图上的权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a little bit different than literally eigenvector centrality, but it's very similar.
zh: 这和字面意义上的特征向量中心性有点不同，但非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we call this technique eigenreviews.
zh: 所以我们把这项技术称为 eigenreviews。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've become convinced that this is more or less the right way to do performance reviews.
zh: 而我已经越来越确信，这基本上就是做绩效评估的正确方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some other tricks that you have to apply to get this to work really well.
zh: 要让它真正运作良好，还需要应用一些其他技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, we apply Dropout where we'll run a thousand iterations where we'll randomly remove some percentage of the edges each iteration.
zh: 比如，我们应用 Dropout，我们会运行一千次迭代，每次迭代随机移除一定百分比的边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when you look at the distribution of scores that you get out of that, if you see additional peaks, for example, this is a clue that there could be voting clicks that need further investigation.
zh: 然后当你看从中得到的分数分布时，如果你看到额外的峰，比如，这是一个线索，说明可能存在需要进一步调查的投票小圈子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a whole, this is, it distributes the judgment across the company, updates more or less continuously with about a month lag, and gives you just way better insight into what's going on really around the company.
zh: 但总体而言，这个方法把判断分布到了整个公司，以大约一个月的延迟或多或少连续地更新，让你对整个公司里真正发生的事情有远远更好的洞察。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is, and it also totally gets rid of that kind of traumatic, super heavy, once a year HR-driven performance review process.
zh: 所以这个，它还完全摆脱了那种一年一次、由 HR 驱动、压力巨大的传统绩效评估流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the point of this talk is not that you should use this in particular, although you should consider it.
zh: 所以这场演讲的重点不是说你们应该特别使用这个方法，尽管你应该考虑一下。
