en: And if you actually roll this out at your company, you can email me and I'll send you a doc with more specific tricks on how to actually get this to work well.
zh: 而且如果你真的在你的公司推行了这套方法，你可以给我发邮件，我会发给你一份文档，里面有关于如何真正让它运作良好的更具体的技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the real theme of the talk...
zh: 但这场演讲真正的主题是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that rate of iteration separates success from failure.
zh: 迭代速度决定了成功与失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can get a fast iteration loop, that really overcomes many other things you're going to run into.
zh: 如果你能获得一个快速迭代循环，它真的能克服你将会遇到的其他许多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this effect is so severe.
zh: 而且这个效应非常严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you can learn one thing every week and there's a competitor that's learning a thing every month, they will never matter.
zh: 我的意思是,如果你每周都能学到一件事,而有一个竞争对手每个月才学到一件事,那他们永远不会有影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overwhelmingly, if you're looking at two different approaches to solve a problem, if there's one that allows you to compound in a much shorter amount of time than the other, even if the other approach has significant redeeming characteristics, you should really consider going with the shorter iteration cycle because the compounding effect is just so dramatic.
zh: 绝大多数情况下,当你在看解决问题的两种不同方法时,如果其中一种能让你在比另一种短得多的时间内实现复利,即使另一种方法有显著的可取之处,你也真的应该考虑选择迭代周期更短的那种,因为复利效应实在是太惊人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So speed determines success and failure and speed is determined by infrastructure.
zh: 所以速度决定成败,而速度由基础设施决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is driven by really boring sounding things like how well do your purchasing and recruiting and spending processes work.
zh: 这取决于一些听起来很无聊的事情,比如你的采购、招聘和支出流程运转得有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is as important as how well do you understand the object level technical content of the thing that you're building.
zh: 这与你在多大程度上理解你所构建事物的对象层面技术内容同样重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see companies founded by just like stellar pedigree scientists and engineers all the time that die on the vine because this execution is tough to follow through when your job is to organize.
zh: 我经常看到由顶级背景的科学家和工程师创立的公司,却半途夭折,因为当你的工作是组织管理时,这种执行很难贯彻下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's uncommon that these deep tech companies fail because the technology doesn't work.
zh: 这些深科技公司失败的原因很少是因为技术行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: They fail because once you end up with this organization of hundreds of people and hundreds of thousands of square feet of physical infrastructure, you haven't built the systems to manage that and it becomes unwieldy, and then you can't make, like, you can't connect strategy to execution.
zh: 它们失败是因为,一旦你最终拥有了一个几百人的组织和几十万平方英尺的实体基础设施,而你还没有建立起管理这一切的系统,它就会变得难以驾驭,然后你就无法……你就无法把战略与执行连接起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we heavily lean towards things that have shorter iteration cycles, kind of, et cetera, like all else equal.
zh: 所以在其他条件相同的情况下,我们强烈倾向于迭代周期更短的东西,等等,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not a blanket rule.
zh: 但这不是一条一刀切的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are no blanket rules in startups.
zh: 在创业公司里没有一刀切的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're looking at each new fact pattern that comes in as its own unique thing and then making decisions that make sense to you.
zh: 你要把每一个进来的新事实模式都看作它自己独特的东西,然后做出对你来说合理的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the harder lessons as a startup founder, one of the harder things I think to really deal with is the fact that you cannot delegate your judgment.
zh: 作为创业公司创始人,更难的教训之一,我认为真正难以应对的事情之一,就是你无法把你的判断委托给别人。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the CEO, you must always make decisions that make sense to you, no matter how much momentum or inertia the alternatives seem to have.
zh: 作为 CEO,你必须始终做出对你来说合理的决策,无论其他选项看起来有多大的势头或惯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in school, let's say there's somebody sitting next to you and you cheat on the test by looking over at them, all else equal, your grade will be dragged towards the average of the class.
zh: 比如在学校里,假设有人坐在你旁边,你靠看他们的答案来考试作弊,在其他条件相同的情况下,你的成绩会被拉向班级的平均水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not good enough to succeed in startups.
zh: 这对在创业公司里取得成功来说是不够好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do things that are at the long tail.
zh: 你必须做那些处于长尾的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The successful companies are the exceptions.
zh: 成功的公司是例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: By becoming an average, that is not good enough.
zh: 通过变成一个平均水平,那是不够好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to succeed, your judgment has to be differentiatedly good.
zh: 为了成功,你的判断必须是差异化地好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the reality might be that you don't know if your judgment is good yet.
zh: 现在,现实可能是你还不知道自己的判断好不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one way or another, you will have to find out.
zh: 所以无论如何,你都必须去弄清楚这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means making decisions that make sense to you, even when you are totally alone in that realization.
zh: 而这意味着做出对你来说合理的决策,即使你在这个认知上完全孤身一人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the only way to get to the really big outcomes.
zh: 这是通往真正巨大成果的唯一途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now it's not that often that everyone else will think one thing and you'll be like, you're all totally wrong, but it is a really eerie feeling.
zh: 并不是经常会发生其他所有人都认为一件事而你却觉得“你们全错了”的情况,但那真的是一种令人毛骨悚然的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you'll get to a point four or five years into the company when there's hundreds of millions of dollars on the line and there's some really high stakes decision and only you can make it.
zh: 比如,你会走到公司成立四五年的那个节点,当时有数亿美元押在上面,有一个非常高风险的决定,而且只有你能做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you will look around for advice.
zh: 然后你会四处寻求建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in the beginning, there's a bunch of things that are easily advised or easily figured out, but you'll get to a key point years in, and you'll look for advice, and there is nobody to ask.
zh: 因为在一开始,有很多事情是容易获得建议或容易弄明白的,但你会走到几年后的一个关键节点,你会寻求建议,却没有人可以问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point, you must have a really good sense of the limits and boundaries of your judgment.
zh: 而在那一刻,你必须对你的判断的极限和边界有一个非常清晰的把握。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a very eerie feeling, and you have to be able to commit to it regardless.
zh: 那是一种非常令人毛骨悚然的感觉,而你必须无论如何都能坚定地做出承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the good news is that, in my experience, it's very difficult to actually get stuck.
zh: 现在,好消息是,根据我的经验,实际上很难真正陷入僵局。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get yourself into trouble, and the action space is always larger than it appears.
zh: 你可能让自己陷入麻烦,而行动空间总是比看起来要大。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of no matter what happens there's usually like when you get like I think it's very easy to try and anticipate all kinds of problems that you'll never actually run into and then you go and do it and then you get to a point where the system like you've run into some real limitation there's always a hundred ideas about how to make it better.
zh: 你可以……无论发生什么,通常就像当你走到……我认为人们很容易试图去预判各种你实际上永远不会遇到的问题,然后你去做,然后你走到一个节点,系统……你遇到了某个真正的限制,而关于如何让它变得更好,总有一百个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is sometimes phrased as action produces information.
zh: 这有时被表述为行动产生信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: This idea is, I think, much deeper than it sounds.
zh: 我认为这个想法比它听起来要深刻得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in physics, there's this quantity called action.
zh: 在物理学中,有一个量叫做作用量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if I throw a ball and it follows a ballistic, like a parabolic trajectory, that trajectory is totally set, like when it leaves my hand, unless it gets blown by wind, some other action is exerted on it, it will follow this ballistic trajectory, which is in a sense like kind of an information minimizing trajectory.
zh: 如果我扔一个球,它遵循一条弹道,比如一条抛物线轨迹,那条轨迹是完全确定的,比如当它离开我的手时,除非被风吹到,或者有其他作用施加在它上面,它就会遵循这条弹道轨迹,这在某种意义上像是一条信息最小化的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can say it just followed, it was ballistic, that totally determines it.
zh: 我可以说它只是遵循了……它是弹道式的,这完全决定了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something else happens, you had to spend some energy time to cause that to happen.
zh: 发生了别的事情,你就必须花费一些能量和时间去促成那件事的发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so whenever you exert action into the universe, that creates information in a very fundamental sense.
zh: 所以每当你向宇宙施加作用,就会在一个非常根本的意义上创造信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And whenever you get stuck, you have to start...
zh: 而每当你陷入僵局,你就必须开始……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like projecting action, producing entropy.
zh: 比如投射行动,产生熵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is, this produces some fairly counterintuitive effects.
zh: 而这,这会产生一些相当反直觉的效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I've seen situations where the company is stuck in a deep local minimum and there's someone who is great in many ways, but it's just the wrong fit for what that company is at the time and removing them, even though they individually are very strong, unblocks the company and allows it to kind of enter a new phase.
zh: 比如我见过这样的情形:公司陷入一个很深的局部极小值,而某个人在很多方面都很出色,但就是与公司当时的状态不匹配,把这个人移走,即使他个人非常强,也能解开公司的阻塞,让公司得以进入一个新阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're, when you get stuck, you have to start doing things.
zh: 当你……当你陷入僵局时,你必须开始行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so,
zh: 所以,

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing underneath the object level content of what the product you are building is, you've got all these support systems.
zh: 在你所构建产品的对象层面内容之下,你还有所有这些支持系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: How the company does purchasing and accounting and recruiting and performance reviews and budgeting and safety and quality is the operating system of the company.
zh: 公司如何做采购、会计、招聘、绩效评估、预算、安全和质量,就是这家公司的操作系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that has a huge impact on how far you can take it.
zh: 而这对你能把它带多远有着巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So speed is determined by infrastructure.
zh: 所以速度由基础设施决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speed determines success and failure.
zh: 速度决定成败。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to put more thought into getting these foundations right.
zh: 你需要多花心思把这些基础做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you do them right at the beginning, everything else is much easier.
zh: 如果你在开始时就做对了,其他一切都会容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you got them wrong, you'll end up spending $5 million a month and feel like you have very little control over it.
zh: 如果你做错了,你最后会每个月花掉 500 万美元,而且感觉自己对它几乎没有控制力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're forced into coarser levers and harder decisions.
zh: 然后你就会被迫使用更粗放的杠杆、做更艰难的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for coming to my TED Talk.
zh: 感谢大家听我的 TED 演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have advice for people trying to choose between industry and academia, starting a company now versus getting a PhD first?
zh: 对于那些在工业界和学术界之间做选择的人,以及现在创业还是先读博士,你有什么建议?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it depends on specifically what you're doing.
zh: 这取决于你具体在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your field only exists in basic research, then getting a PhD might be very reasonable.
zh: 如果你的领域只存在于基础研究中,那么读博士可能是很合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when things really start to work,
zh: 所以当事情真正开始运转起来的时候,

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, if 20 years ago, the best computer scientists were at CMU and Harvard, and 50 years ago, the best rocket, like, if you wanted to work on rocket engines, you were at NASA, you were at a university, you were at University of Maryland or somewhere, and now they're at, now the best computer scientists are at Google and Apple and OpenAI.
zh: 比如,20 年前,最好的计算机科学家在 CMU 和哈佛;50 年前,最好的火箭——比如,如果你想研究火箭发动机,你会去 NASA,会去大学,会去马里兰大学或某个地方;而现在,现在最好的计算机科学家在 Google、Apple 和 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the best rocket scientists are at SpaceX and Blue Origin and others.
zh: 而最好的火箭科学家在 SpaceX 和 Blue Origin 以及其他公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when a field really starts to work, industry can just marshal such larger levels of resources and can just move so much faster.
zh: 所以当一个领域真正开始运转起来时,工业界能够调动的资源规模要大得多,而且推进速度要快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question has been, why has academia stayed so relevant in the life sciences?
zh: 于是问题就来了:为什么学术界在生命科学领域仍然如此重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reality is that it doesn't work that well for most things.
zh: 现实是,对大多数事情来说,它运转得并不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans just aren't that good at drug discovery.
zh: 人类就是不太擅长药物发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if your field is really only in academia, then it can make total sense to get a PhD.
zh: 所以如果你的领域真的只在学术界,那么读博士就完全说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, you know, a lot of...
zh: 我觉得,你知道,很多……

speaker: Unknown
en: It is uncommon that startups don't get the technology to work.
zh: 创业公司搞不定技术,这种情况并不常见。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is more common that they can't organize the human organizations to accomplish their goals.
zh: 更常见的是,他们无法组织好人类组织来实现自己的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And learning, that is also a skill set, the only way to learn it.
zh: 而学习——那也是一种技能——是学习它的唯一途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's an oral tradition.
zh: 我认为这是一种口传心授的传统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do it.
zh: 你必须亲手去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if the choice is working at a really high-performing company adjacent to where you want to be versus getting a PhD, I'd probably recommend the company.
zh: 所以如果选择是在一家非常高绩效、离你想去的地方很近的公司工作,还是去读博士,我可能更推荐去公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not an absolute rule, and it really depends on the field.
zh: 但这不是绝对的规则,真的取决于领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: What counts as evidence of exceptional ability to you?
zh: 对你来说,什么才算得上卓越能力的证据?

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything that concretely you can put your finger on that separates that person from their high school class.
zh: 任何你能具体指出来、能把这个人跟他高中同学区分开的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have your average high school student, we just want some concrete fact that...
zh: 如果你有一个普通的高中生,我们只想要某个具体的事实……

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, the best evidence of exceptional ability is our winning at legible competitive games.
zh: 理想情况下,卓越能力最好的证据是在清晰可见的竞技比赛中获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this could be...
zh: 这可以是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Being like a chess grandmaster.
zh: 比如成为国际象棋特级大师。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be winning design build fly or formula SAE competitions.
zh: 可以是赢得 Design Build Fly 或 Formula SAE 竞赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of Silicon Valley deep tech companies that are basically built out of formula SAE winners from college, people that just spent their college experience building things and racing them and finding out.
zh: 有一批硅谷深科技公司基本上就是由大学里 Formula SAE 的优胜者建立起来的,那些人整个大学经历就是在造东西、比赛、然后发现问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to have that type of competitive feedback.
zh: 我认为你必须有那种类型的竞争反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is tough to know if you're exceptional without having some legible competitive game.
zh: 如果没有一个清晰可见的竞技比赛,很难知道自己是否卓越。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we hire engineers now?
zh: 我们现在怎么招聘工程师?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we still use leet code or do we have better ways?
zh: 我们还在用 leet code 吗,还是有了更好的方法?

speaker: Unknown
en: If we allow AI use, how do you understand the skills of the applicant?
zh: 如果允许使用 AI,你怎么了解应聘者的技能?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've never, I don't think we've ever really used leet code.
zh: 我们从来没有——我不认为我们真的用过 leet code。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe some other people on the team do it in secret, but I've never asked it.
zh: 也许团队里有些其他人偷偷在用,但我从来没要求过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So software in particular
zh: 软件这个领域尤其如此,

speaker: Unknown
en: The rewards to horsepower are so great that it really is just, it's a field that attracts really smart people because it gives you this very rapid feedback.
zh: 算力带来的回报太大了,以至于它确实是一个能吸引真正聪明人的领域,因为它给你非常快速的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you think about, like there's a lot of really smart people in biology, but when you have a biological idea, it can take you many months to find out if it's a good one.
zh: 比如,你想想,生物学里也有很多非常聪明的人,但当你有了一个生物学想法,可能要花好几个月才能知道它是不是个好想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In software, if you have an idea, you can often build it in a couple hours or you can get feedback within days.
zh: 而在软件领域,如果你有一个想法,你常常可以在几个小时内把它做出来,或者在几天内得到反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it has this really addictive feedback loop, kind of like high frequency trading that just draws in really smart people.
zh: 所以它有一个非常令人上瘾的反馈循环,有点像高频交易,能把真正聪明的人吸引进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we look for kind of over your life, what signals do we have that you have done something interesting?
zh: 所以我们看的是,纵观你的人生,我们有哪些信号表明你做成过什么有意思的事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's uncommon for someone to get into their mid-20s without there being some thing in their background that they went out and sought out and did.
zh: 比如,一个人到了二十五六岁,背景里却没有任何一件他自己主动去寻找并做成的事,这是不常见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is like such an open-ended criteria.
zh: 但这是一个非常开放的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can really be anything.
zh: 它真的可以是任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't...
zh: 我们不……

speaker: Unknown
en: More directly to the question, we increasingly don't directly evaluate programming.
zh: 更直接地回答这个问题,我们越来越不直接评估编程能力了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We try to evaluate thinking.
zh: 我们尝试评估的是思考能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is design questions.
zh: 比如这是设计类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if we give you a domain, how do you break it down?
zh: 比如如果我们给你一个领域,你怎么把它拆解?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you understand the decomposition of the problem clearly?
zh: 你能不能清晰地理解问题的拆解方式?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really measures of like, can you think clearly rather than can you write code?
zh: 这实际上衡量的是,你能不能清晰地思考,而不是你能不能写代码?

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you take away from your experience at Neuralink?
zh: 你从 Neuralink 的经历中收获了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question of like, should you go get a PhD?
zh: 所以这个问题就像,你要不要去读个博士?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have a PhD.
zh: 我没有博士学位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spent five years running a company for...
zh: 我花了五年时间为……经营一家公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: My CEO at Neuralink.
zh: 我的 Neuralink CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest lessons, I think, is that there are few really generic
zh: 我认为最大的教训之一是,很少有真正通用性的东西,

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no generic algorithm for how to succeed at a startup.
zh: 没有一个通用的算法能告诉你如何在创业公司取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no set of five bullet points that can be conveyed that if you just turn the crank, your company will be successful.
zh: 没有哪五个要点,你照着执行公司就能成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a long series of judgment calls.
zh: 这是一长连串的判断取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the most important thing is that those filters are tuned really well.
zh: 所以最重要的是,那些过滤器被调得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think one of the most valuable things for me at Neuralink was I was working with someone who has empirically excellent judgment.
zh: 所以我认为在 Neuralink 对我最有价值的事情之一是,我和一个经验证判断力极其出色的人共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could get into trouble together and there'd be all...
zh: 我们可以一起陷入麻烦,然后会有各种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Something would happen and there'd be two possible solutions that would make sense.
zh: 某件事发生,会有两个看似都说得通的解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd go to him and say, like, is it option A or is it option B?
zh: 我会去找他说,比如,是选项 A 还是选项 B?

speaker: Unknown
en: He'd look at it and be like, oh, it's definitely option B.
zh: 他看一眼就会说,哦,肯定是选项 B。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem would never recur.
zh: 那个问题再也不会出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And having been in those situations where I was trying to make these bets with stakes attached, looking forward in time, not getting feedback until later, with that advice was incredibly useful for fitting those filters.
zh: 在那些我要下注、附带实际利害、向前看却要过很久才能得到反馈的情境中,有那样的建议对于调校那些过滤器极其有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't know that there was really a shortcut.
zh: 而且我不确定是否真的有捷径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that just hearing the stories when you're not there, really thinking about it because there are real stakes, and then getting that feedback.
zh: 我觉得就是当你不在现场时听那些故事,真正去思考,因为背后有真实的利害,然后得到那种反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is an essential part of the education of an entrepreneur that I think many people underrate.
zh: 这是创业者教育中不可或缺的一部分,我认为很多人低估了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is really worth working for a company that has an excellent culture that you respect before jumping right into your own startup.
zh: 我认为在直接跳进自己的创业公司之前,先去一家拥有你敬重的优秀文化的公司工作,是非常值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is relatively uncommon that startup cultures get rediscovered entirely from first principles.
zh: 创业公司文化完全从第一性原理被重新发现的情况相对少见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually they're passed down as, again, oral traditions because there's a founding team that worked at another company which worked at another company and so they inherited it.
zh: 通常它们是作为口口相传的传统被传递下来的,因为有一个创始团队曾在另一家公司工作,那家公司又源自另一家公司,所以他们继承了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or in some cases where there's really a breakout where there's just some market dislocation that it really enables.
zh: 或者在某些真正爆发的案例中,出现了某种市场错位,真正提供了机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: A team kind of out of nowhere to build it.
zh: 让一支仿佛凭空出现的团队把它建立起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll often get it from the VCs.
zh: 他们通常会从 VC 那里得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's working with the people that have that judgment so that you can get that reinforcement learning as its long series of facts is really important.
zh: 但关键在于与拥有那种判断力的人共事,这样你才能获得那种强化学习,因为它是一长串的事实,这一点非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could BCIs or neural interfaces help us figure out what consciousness actually is?
zh: 脑机接口或神经接口能帮助我们弄清楚意识究竟是什么吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: How?
zh: 怎么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the end of the artificial intelligence quest is super intelligent machines, I think the end of the BCI quest is conscious machines.
zh: 如果人工智能探索的终点是超级智能机器,我认为脑机接口探索的终点是有意识的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brain is composed of ordinary matter arranged according to the rules of chemistry, only things found on the periodic table.
zh: 大脑由普通物质构成,按照化学规则排列,只包含元素周期表上能找到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems tough to believe that there's like some new physics going on in there.
zh: 相信里面有什么新的物理学在起作用,似乎很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: We're looking for some mapping between the substrate activity and the phenomenal content.
zh: 我们在寻找底层活动与现象内容之间的某种映射。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if we had a magical BCI that allowed me to see the instant state of every neuron in the brain and drive them, I think we'd figure out consciousness pretty fast.
zh: 现在,如果我们有一个魔法般的脑机接口,能让我看到大脑中每个神经元的即时状态并驱动它们,我想我们会很快搞清楚意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is a practical problem, not a philosophical problem.
zh: 我认为这是一个实践问题,而不是哲学问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to prove it, but first of all, that practical problem is real, and we'll have to do this stuff in humans.
zh: 但要证明它,首先,那个实践问题是真实的,我们将必须在人类身上做这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to prove any of this, we'll have to do it in humans.
zh: 而要证明这些中的任何一点,我们都必须在人类身上做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that it is possible that you could use a BCI to prove it.
zh: 我认为有可能用脑机接口来证明它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have some ideas about how to do those experiments, but they are still some number of years off, right?
zh: 我们对如何做那些实验有一些想法,但它们还有若干年的距离,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The things going into humans now are not designed to study consciousness.
zh: 现在进入人体的那些设备并不是为研究意识而设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think that that is further down this path.
zh: 但我确实认为那是这条路径上更远的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What should I study to contribute to BCIs?
zh: 我应该学习什么才能为 BCI(脑机接口)做出贡献？

speaker: Unknown
en: This really depends on your background.
zh: 这真的取决于你的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Neural interfaces are a very interdisciplinary problem.
zh: 神经接口是一个非常跨领域的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It uses everything from stem cell biology to materials in microfabrication to software to animal behavior to surgery.
zh: 它用到了从干细胞生物学、微加工材料、软件、动物行为到手术的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are many different entry points in it.
zh: 所以它有很多不同的切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things that we found is that it's better to have a smaller team that can fit more of the problem in their heads and then compress it together.
zh: 我们发现的一件事是，最好有一个更小的团队，能让更多的人把问题装进脑子里，然后再把它压缩到一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Contrast this to how academia usually handles interdisciplinary problems where they'll have an interdisciplinary center that pulls in very deep verticalized experts who are kind of meet at the center.
zh: 与此相对的是学术界通常处理跨领域问题的方式，他们会设立一个跨领域中心，拉来非常垂直化的深度专家，让他们在中心处会合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem is that they're all speaking different languages.
zh: 而问题在于，他们说的都是不同的语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's often hard to really...
zh: 所以通常很难真正……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like even when they can communicate, typically you end up shipping the interfaces of those departments.
zh: 比如即使他们能够沟通，通常你最终交付的是那些部门的接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas for us, if we can kind of hold the problem in the head of a smaller number of people, we can shift around where the bottlenecks are.
zh: 而对我们来说，如果我们能让更少的人把问题装在脑子里，我们就可以在瓶颈所在之处灵活移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specific example of this is our protein engineering group has been able to develop much more sensitive, like much better proteins for some things that we need to do, which has allowed us to relax some electronics requirements.
zh: 一个具体的例子是我们的蛋白质工程团队已经能够开发出更灵敏的、在某些我们需要做的事情上好得多的蛋白质，这让我们得以放松一些电子方面的要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we have, so specifically we have proteins called opsins, they allow us to make neurons light sensitive.
zh: 具体来说，我们有一种叫做视蛋白的蛋白质，它们让我们能够让神经元对光敏感。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that if we shine light on them, we can fire a neuron.
zh: 这样如果我们用光照射它们，就能让一个神经元放电。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem was that you needed to hit a neuron with a lot of light to fire it, which means that you can't have that many light sources because it gets too hot.
zh: 问题在于，你需要用很多光照射神经元才能让它放电，这意味着你不能有太多光源，因为会太热。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've been able to make the protein more sensitive, which means that we can have more LEDs because each one can be dimmer.
zh: 所以我们已经能让这种蛋白质更灵敏，这意味着我们可以有更多的 LED，因为每一个都可以更暗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've turned this electronics problem into a biology problem that allowed us to relax those constraints.
zh: 于是我们把一个电子学问题变成了一个生物学问题，这让我们得以放松那些约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get that as much when you have these interdisciplinary centers where there's like one group focused on one thing, there's another group focused on another thing.
zh: 当你拥有这些跨领域中心时，你就不太能得到这种效果——一个组专注于一件事，另一个组专注于另一件事。 [[408 已在上面]]

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would say being able to have a broader perspective of more of the problem is really valuable.
zh: 所以我想说，能够对问题的更多部分拥有更宽广的视角是非常宝贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just really as deep and clear an understanding of the system as you can get.
zh: 然后就是对这个系统尽可能深入和清晰的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's no substitute for being hands-on.
zh: 我认为没有什么能替代亲自动手。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't really matter.
zh: 具体是哪一样其实不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want some hard skill to get you in the door, software, electronics, mechanical, materials, something.
zh: 你需要某项硬技能来帮你敲开大门，软件、电子、机械、材料，随便什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then from there, I would try to learn as much of it as you can.
zh: 然后从那里开始，我会建议你尽可能多地学习这个领域的其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does an AI replace in scientific research?
zh: AI 在科学研究中取代的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are humans still necessary, if anywhere?
zh: 人类在哪些地方(如果还有的话)仍然是必需的？

speaker: Unknown
en: We still definitely need humans.
zh: 我们肯定仍然需要人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in scientific research in particular, I mean, it's tough to predict.
zh: 尤其是在科学研究中，我是说，这很难预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like AI is clearly advancing very rapidly.
zh: 比如 AI 显然在非常快速地进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that you need to think about how to have your company be AI native in the sense that every, like you want to gather all of the context, all of the stuff happening in your company and be able to make that available efficiently to agents because those are clearly a big part of the future.
zh: 我确实认为你需要思考如何让你的公司是 AI 原生的，也就是说，你想收集公司里发生的所有上下文、所有的事情，并能够高效地把这些提供给智能体，因为它们显然是未来很大的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us in Helix, really everything goes in there.
zh: 所以对我们来说，在 Helix 里，真的是所有东西都放进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the reasons that we did that was because...
zh: 我们这么做的原因之一是因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just is it powerful to have everything in one database to link together, purchasing to quality to batch records and manufacturing so that we can trace stuff more efficiently, but also so that we could give it all to agents.
zh: 不仅仅是因为把所有东西放在一个数据库里串联起来很强大——把采购、质量、批次记录和制造连起来，这样我们能更高效地追溯东西——还因为我们可以把这一切都交给智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we found them to be a multiplier for the team, not a replacement.
zh: 所以我们发现它们是团队的乘数，而不是替代品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The three biggest areas that AI has had an impact for us so far are...
zh: 到目前为止，AI 对我们影响最大的三个领域是……

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, coding.
zh: 首先，写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've written a lot of code in my life.
zh: 我这辈子写过很多代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I've looked at the source very much the last six months.
zh: 我觉得最近六个月我没怎么看过源代码了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is getting really good.
zh: 这方面正在变得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Regulations.
zh: 法规。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is...
zh: 所以这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're doing anything really interesting, you're going to end up regulated, and then you'll probably end up dealing with these things called quality systems.
zh: 所以如果你在做任何真正有意思的事情，你最终都会受到监管，然后你很可能就要对付这些叫做质量体系的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a quality system, I think, triggers a lot of scar tissue for people because it's just the quintessential heavy bureaucracy, slow everything down.
zh: 质量体系这个概念，我想，会触发很多人的伤疤组织，因为它就是典型的重型官僚主义，把一切都拖慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea of quality itself is actually not a problem.
zh: 质量本身这个理念其实不是问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that humans are bad at reading and interpreting these things.
zh: 问题在于人类不擅长阅读和解释这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we make a product, one of the things we have to do is identify all of the standards that might apply.
zh: 所以当我们做一个产品时，我们必须做的事情之一就是识别所有可能适用的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's standards for everything.
zh: 而什么都有标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's standards for how the lithium-ion batteries plug into a PCB.
zh: 有关于锂离子电池如何插入 PCB 的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's standards for...
zh: 还有关于……

speaker: Unknown
en: Electrical insulation of the boards.
zh: 电路板的电气绝缘的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's standards for shipping labels.
zh: 运输标签是有标准的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, you'll have to take your shipping packaging, print a label on it, and put it in a Vibe box and show that the corners of the label don't curl in a way that might cause it to attach.
zh: 到某个时候,你得拿着你的运输包装,在上面打印一个标签,放进一个 Vibe 箱子里,并证明标签的角不会以可能导致脱落的方式卷起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you hire regulatory experts to go find all of the standards that might apply, make a list of them, and then have a spreadsheet which is all of the evidence that you comply with all of the standards.
zh: 所以你要雇监管专家去找出所有可能适用的标准,列一个清单,然后做一个电子表格,里面全是你符合所有标准的证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have this...
zh: 于是你就有了这个……

speaker: Unknown
en: This thing can take many, many months historically.
zh: 这件事在历史上可能要花很多很多个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI has totally transformed it.
zh: AI 已经彻底改变了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we can very quickly look up all the standards.
zh: 我的意思是,我们可以非常快速地查出所有的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can very quickly generate the evidence tables.
zh: 我们可以非常快速地生成证据表格。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that to the degree that there's kind of over...
zh: 而且我认为,从某种程度上说,存在某种过度……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we definitely need to deregulate some things, but I think that the combination of AI and regulation is a better fit than people think.
zh: 我的意思是,我们确实需要对一些东西放松监管,但我认为 AI 和监管的结合比人们想象的更匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can use it to smooth a lot of stuff where the regulations are written in blood and largely good ideas.
zh: 你可以用它来理顺很多事情,在这些事情上,法规是用血写成的,而且大体上是好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just hard for humans to do it.
zh: 只是对人类来说做起来太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why build your own infrastructure platforms rather than just buying them?
zh: 为什么要构建自己的基础设施平台,而不是直接买现成的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can't really buy these things.
zh: 恰恰相反,现在有很多例子,公司是围绕一块真正只为他们量身定制的软件成长起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are ERP systems out there, but there's no company that loves their ERP system.
zh: 市面上有 ERP 系统,但没有哪家公司爱他们的 ERP 系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if there's anyone who's really like, I want to spend more time in NetSuite.
zh: 我不知道是否真的有人会说,我想在 NetSuite 里多花点时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the contrary, there are a bunch of examples now of companies that grow up around a piece of software that's really fit just for them.
zh: 相反，现在有很多例子，公司是围绕一个真正只适合他们的软件成长起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like YC, famously, has a lot of internal software that I think really makes YC work.
zh: 比如 YC,出了名地拥有很多内部软件,我认为这些软件真正让 YC 得以运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook also very famously invested heavily in internal tools and now has like I think gets a lot of efficiency from that.
zh: Facebook 也非常出名地在内部工具上投入巨资,而现在我认为它从中获得了很多效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: SpaceX and Tesla internally have a pretty giant piece of software called Warp Speed that runs a lot of their manufacturing and R&D processes.
zh: SpaceX 和 Tesla 内部有一个相当庞大的软件,叫 Warp Speed,管理着他们大量的制造和研发流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when one company grows up around like a harness fit to it, it can be very powerful.
zh: 所以当一家公司围绕一个适合它的挽具成长起来时,这可能非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is powerful in a way that the software that you can buy isn't.
zh: 它的强大之处在于,你买得到的软件做不到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this requires you to really look into the future, because certainly, especially at the seed stage, this is not the thing that you would think you should be focusing on.
zh: 但这需要你真正展望未来,因为尤其是在种子阶段,这不是你会认为自己应该专注于的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And historically, it has not been.
zh: 而且在历史上,确实也不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a thing that has changed with agents.
zh: 而这是一件随着智能体出现而改变的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that you can vibe code this now makes it a reasonable thing to think about.
zh: 现在你可以用 vibe coding 把它做出来,这让这件事成为一个值得考虑的合理选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, software has been so expensive, you would have had to buy it.
zh: 在历史上,软件太昂贵了,你只能买。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what everybody did for a long time.
zh: 很长一段时间里,大家都是这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was, I think, a worse world.
zh: 我认为,那是一个更糟的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that world has changed.
zh: 而那个世界已经改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now there are better options available.
zh: 所以现在有更好的选择可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like I said, it's like we previously had used, we used Greenhouse.
zh: 但就像我说的,就像我们之前用过的,我们用过 Greenhouse。

speaker: Unknown
en: Greenhouse required us to have a small number of people as a bottleneck at that first funnel stage.
zh: Greenhouse 要求我们在第一道漏斗阶段让少数几个人成为瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Placing that with software, we were able to explore voting mechanisms and fairly detailed voting mechanisms that can make smart inferences about who would know about an applicant, things that you can't really do with the commercial software.
zh: 用软件替代它之后,我们得以探索投票机制,相当精细的投票机制,能够对谁会了解某位申请者做出聪明的推断,这些是商用软件做不到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for a lot of these processes, you should think about how you want it to work for you.
zh: 所以对于很多这类流程,你应该思考你希望它如何为你服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are human organizations, these human processes that have to be staffed.
zh: 这些是人类组织,这些必须有人 staffing 的人类流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they aren't done routinely, it will atrophy.
zh: 如果不经常执行,它就会萎缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's things that make sense for different teams and founders in the way that they view the world and think about it.
zh: 而对于不同团队和创始人,基于他们看待和思考世界的方式,有些事情是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really is all very different.
zh: 它真的全都非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you build a thing that works for you and then you bake that into the company so when you put something there, it stays there, it can be very, very useful.
zh: 但如果你造出一个对你有用的东西,然后把它烙进公司,这样你放进去的东西就会留在那里,它可以非常、非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: What changes should we expect in the world?
zh: 我们应该期待世界上发生什么变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: As BCIs start to work and get widely adopted, do intelligence differences no longer matter?
zh: 当 BCI 开始奏效并被广泛采用时,智力差异是否不再重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's this meme that BCI is an artificial intelligence adjacent story, and there's some of that.
zh: 所以有这样一个梗,说 BCI 是一个与人工智能相邻的故事,确实有几分道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like eventually, like if AI is building super intelligent machines and BCI labs are building conscious machines and we're building brain-to-brain connections so that the boundaries between those things become less meaningful.
zh: 比如最终,如果 AI 在建造超级智能的机器,而 BCI 实验室在建造有意识的机器,而我们在建造脑对脑的连接,这样这些东西之间的边界就变得不那么有意义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like at some point you want a super intelligent, conscious machine that we can participate in, but that actually feels further away to me.
zh: 比如到某个时候,你会想要一台我们能参与其中的超级智能、有意识的机器,但那对我来说实际上还更遥远。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the near term, BCI is really a longevity story.
zh: 我认为在短期内,BCI 真正是一个长寿的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I view longevity as really just healthcare.
zh: 而我把长寿看作真的就是医疗保健。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, just biotech.
zh: 我的意思是,就是生物科技。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that it hasn't, like, I think it is not right to say that the pharma companies or any of these, like, past healthcare companies are not interested in cures.
zh: 只不过它还没有……比如,我认为说制药公司或任何这些过去的医疗保健公司对治愈不感兴趣是不对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that is what all of them want.
zh: 我认为那正是它们所有人想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that that's been beyond our capabilities.
zh: 只不过这超出了我们的能力范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in neural engineering, the people here, BCI, I think they think of
zh: 在神经工程领域，这里的人，BCI,我认为他们想的是

speaker: Unknown
en: Motor decoding, like I put some electrodes in motor cortex and now they can control it like a video game.
zh: 运动解码，比如我把一些电极放进运动皮层，现在他们就能像玩电子游戏一样控制它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think neural engineering is much broader than that.
zh: 我认为神经工程比这广泛得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We include our retinal prosthesis in that.
zh: 我们把我们的视网膜假体也包括在内。

speaker: Unknown
en: We include cochlear implants in that.
zh: 我们把人工耳蜗也包括在内。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this...
zh: 而这……

speaker: Unknown
en: This, I think, is a contrarian take on all of healthcare.
zh: 这个，我认为，是对整个医疗保健的一个反主流观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gives you these effect sizes that you just don't really see in medicine.
zh: 它给你带来这些你在医学中真正看不到的效应量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you have a patient on a dopaminergic drug for Parkinson's, that works for some period of time, but it's a relatively small effect after a little while.
zh: 比如如果你给帕金森病患者服用多巴胺能药物，它会在一段时间内起作用，但过一阵子之后效果相对较小。

speaker: Unknown
en: You turn on a deep brain stimulator and a patient goes from not being able to hold a cup of water to being able to write cursive in like 10 seconds.
zh: 你打开脑深部刺激器，患者在大约 10 秒内从无法端起一杯水变成能够写连笔字。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to talk about strong patient testimonials, you should see a newborn having their cochlear implant turned on.
zh: 如果你想谈谈强有力的患者见证，你应该看看一个新生儿的人工耳蜗被打开的那一刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you deal directly with the brain as a computer, not only do you not have to solve some of these really hard biology problems that are just beyond humanity's capabilities, but you get these results pretty readily that, again, you can get an engineering gradient, you can get them more reliably, and they're just large effects.
zh: 当你直接把大脑当作计算机来处理时，你不仅不必解决那些远远超出人类能力的真正困难的生物学问题，而且你能相当轻易地得到这些结果，再说一次，你可以得到一个工程梯度，你可以更可靠地得到它们，而且它们就是大效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I see this as a way to extend and improve the life of everybody.
zh: 所以我把这看作是延长和改善每个人生命的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brain is the thing that makes you you.
zh: 大脑是让你成为你的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the only thing that in principle you can't transplant.
zh: 它是原则上你无法移植的唯一东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get a new heart or a new liver.
zh: 你可以换一颗新心脏或一个新肝脏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot even in principle get a new brain.
zh: 但即使原则上你也无法换一个新大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the brain is usually not the thing that fails.
zh: 而且大脑通常不是那个出问题的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can deal with the brain directly, I think this is going to...
zh: 所以如果你能直接处理大脑，我认为这将会……

speaker: Unknown
en: This is more of a radical longevity story than it is an AI one for the moment, although all of these things will come together over some period of time.
zh: 目前这更像是一个激进的寿命延长故事，而不是一个 AI 故事，尽管所有这些东西会在某个时期内汇聚到一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: For your eigenreview performance system, how do you prevent employees from colluding on their votes or downvoting somebody on purpose?
zh: 对于你的特征回顾绩效系统，你如何防止员工在投票上串通，或者故意给某人投反对票？

speaker: Unknown
en: So as I mentioned, there are some tricks.
zh: 正如我所提到的，有一些技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, applying Markov Chain Monte Carlo Dropout allows us to detect things like voting clicks.
zh: 比如，应用马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛 Dropout 让我们能够检测诸如投票点击之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because now instead of seeing one peak, you'll see two peaks.
zh: 因为现在你看到的不是一个峰，而是两个峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a clue to look in.
zh: 那就是一个值得深入查看的线索。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll look into that.
zh: 我会去调查那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's designed to be tolerant of these things.
zh: 我的意思是，它的设计本来就是容忍这些事情的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is really fairly transparent.
zh: 我认为它确实相当透明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also not our only signal.
zh: 它也不是我们唯一的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of several.
zh: 它是若干信号之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anybody's interested in this, send me an email and I will share a document with the specific tricks.
zh: 如果有人对这个感兴趣，给我发邮件，我会分享一份包含具体技巧的文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to understand a little more about how you were going to deploy it first.
zh: 但我想多了解一点你最初打算如何部署它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of this is tradecraft.
zh: 这其中有些是行业诀窍。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're building something as long horizon as neurotech, how do you figure out how much runway you actually need to keep the company alive?
zh: 当你在构建神经科技这样长周期的东西时，你如何确定要让公司活下去实际上需要多少 runway?

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you get investors to fund that much?
zh: 你又如何让投资者为这么多钱出资？

speaker: Unknown
en: So sometimes, I mean, you often see founders, especially more experienced ones, pitching VCs for what they think is reasonable to ask for rather than what they need to run the experiment.
zh: 有时候，我的意思是，你经常看到创始人，尤其是更有经验的创始人，向 VC 融资时报的是他们认为合理可要的数额，而不是他们运行实验所需的数额。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're raising some amount of money to go find out some answer.
zh: 你融资一定数额的钱是为了去找出某个答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to that might be no, the investors understand this.
zh: 那个答案可能是否定的，投资者明白这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like depending on what business you're in, but you have to actually run the experiment.
zh: 比如这取决于你身处什么行业，但你必须真正去运行那个实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things, like there are definitely some ideas that are worth funding with $50 million or $0, but not $5 million.
zh: 其中一件事是，确实有一些想法值得用 5000 万美元或 0 美元来资助，但不值得用 500 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: You won't run the experiment.
zh: 你没法运行那个实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be a really frustrating experience.
zh: 那会是一次非常令人沮丧的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll get an ambiguous outcome.
zh: 你会得到一个模棱两可的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my first piece of advice is you should figure out what you think it's going to take to actually run the experiment, which is not the whole company.
zh: 所以我的第一条建议是，你应该弄清楚你认为真正运行实验需要什么，这不是整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is, what is your next value inflection point?
zh: 也就是说，你的下一个价值拐点是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: No matter how ambitious and open-ended of your plan is, you should have some sense of what is your next key value inflection point?
zh: 无论你的计划多么雄心勃勃、多么开放，你应该对以下问题有所认识：你的下一个关键价值拐点是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the experiments that need to go into that?
zh: 有哪些实验需要投入其中？

speaker: Unknown
en: Price that out and then raise twice the money.
zh: 把它算出价格，然后融两倍的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean...
zh: 所以，我是说……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some amount of waste, I think, if you can get waste down to 20 or 30%, that's pretty good.
zh: 我觉得会有一定程度的浪费,如果你能把浪费降到 20% 或 30%,那已经相当不错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, the advice is figure out what it costs to actually run the experiment, raise twice that, and raise that or not.
zh: 总之,建议是:弄清楚真正运行这个实验需要花多少钱,按两倍去融资,然后融或者不融。

speaker: Unknown
en: Beyond that, you'll always discover new things.
zh: 除此之外,你总是会 discover 新的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's usually some path through the mess.
zh: 通常总有一条穿过这团乱麻的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you start the company, you're not going to get a guarantee that you won't be on a bridge to nowhere or that it will work on the funding that you have.
zh: 但当你创立公司的时候,你不会得到任何保证,保证你不会走上一座通往 nowhere 的桥,或者保证它能在你手头的资金下跑通。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to have to get in there and figure it out halfway through.
zh: 你将不得不深入其中,在半路上把它弄明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that people should push for profitability sooner than they often think that they need to.
zh: 我认为人们应该比他们通常以为自己需要的时间更早去追求盈利。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, I mean, even though we are seen as this, I think, very open-ended, deep tech company with a very long roadmap, which is true, we are also relentlessly focused on revenue at this point.
zh: 对我们来说,我是说,尽管我们被视为一家非常开放式、路线图非常长的 deep tech 公司——这确实是事实——但在这一点上,我们也毫不松懈地聚焦于收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are trying to get to sustainability.
zh: 我们在努力走向可持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like, I mean, the company is kind of constantly dying slowly of this money cancer that we can beat into remission every couple of years with the fundraising, but then it eventually comes back and I want that feeling to be over.
zh: 感觉上,我是说,公司就像在不断地缓慢死于一种金钱癌症,我们每隔几年靠融资把它打到缓解期,但它最终会回来,我想让这种感觉结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so no matter how big of a problem or big of a vision it feels, you do need to think about how do you get to revenue so that not just you can do it forever, but then you'll be valued on your long-term roadmap, not valued on your probability of dying.
zh: 所以无论这个问题或愿景看起来有多大,你确实需要思考如何获得收入,这样不仅你能永远做下去,而且你会按你的长期路线图被估值,而不是按你的死亡概率被估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it really opens up an
zh: 而且它真的会打开

speaker: Unknown
en: Another side of investors that wouldn't be relevant otherwise.
zh: 投资人的另一面,那在别的情况下是不会显现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the best piece of advice you've received?
zh: 你收到过的最好的建议是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've acquired way too much brain damage over the last 20 years to have a memory capable of picking that out.
zh: 过去 20 年我积累了太多脑损伤,已经没有能力从记忆里挑出那一条了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think if other than speed being the basis of success and infrastructure determines your speed, it is important to appreciate that there are no general principles.
zh: 我是说,我认为,除了“速度是成功的基础,而基础设施决定你的速度”之外,很重要的一点是要认识到:不存在通用原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people are looking for shortcuts.
zh: 我觉得人们总是在找捷径。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are looking for...
zh: 人们在找……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a pithy set of instructions that are like, oh, I figured it out.
zh: 就像一套精炼的守则,像是“哦,我搞明白了”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that doesn't exist.
zh: 那种东西不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like every one of these things is different.
zh: 每一个这样的案例都是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you get to that moment in history, you're doing something new.
zh: 当你走到历史的那个时刻,你在做一件新的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we can take, we can reflect for a second on how crazy it is that all, that this is possible.
zh: 我是说,我们可以稍微反思一下,这一切成为可能是多么疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like for the vast majority of human history, if you were a smart 20 year old that like had an idea to like make your society better and you raise this to the people with capital, the reaction was like, you should pay attention to the harvest.
zh: 就像在人类历史的绝大部分时间里,如果你是一个聪明的 20 岁年轻人,有了一个让自己的社会变得更好的想法,你把它讲给有钱人听,反应会是:你应该去关心收成。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that it is not widely available, it's not universally available, but it's not widely available that if you're a really smart 20-year-old, you can come to San Francisco and make the case, and if it's an interesting idea, you'll get millions of dollars to find out.
zh: 事实是它并非广泛可得,它不是普遍可得的,但它并非广泛可得——如果你是一个非常聪明的 20 岁年轻人,你可以来到 San Francisco 陈述你的理由,如果这是个有趣的想法,你就会得到数百万美元去把它弄个明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not the case for most of the world today, and it's certainly not the case for most of history anywhere.
zh: 今天世界上的大部分地方并非如此,而且在历史上的大部分时间里的任何地方都肯定不是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that shouldn't feel normal.
zh: 但这不应该让人觉得是常态。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is given to push the frontier out.
zh: 这是被给予的,用来把前沿往外推。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're on the frontier, they're like...
zh: 而当你在前沿上,他们就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: You're figuring it out as you go.
zh: 你是在边走边把它弄明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the job.
zh: 这就是这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would try to rely less on things that feel like startup advice and more on how good is your judgment?
zh: 所以我会尽量少依赖那些听起来像创业建议的东西,更多地去问:你的判断力有多好?

speaker: Unknown
en: How well is that refined in your domain?
zh: 在你的领域里,它被磨砺得有多好?

speaker: Unknown
en: And remembering that you have to think for yourself.
zh: 并且记住:你必须独立思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the hardest remaining engineering challenges involved in getting BCIs to work?
zh: 让 BCI 跑通还剩哪些最难的工程挑战?

speaker: Unknown
en: So in BCIs, we often feel very limited by power and thermal constraints on the implants.
zh: 在 BCI 领域,我们经常感到非常受限于植入体上的功耗和散热约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this creates a strong pressure to implant as little as possible and do the rest off the body.
zh: 这就造成了很强的压力:尽量少往体内植入,把其余的放到体外完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't pass a wire through the skin because the skin is a very important immune barrier.
zh: 你不能让一根导线穿过皮肤,因为皮肤是一个非常重要的免疫屏障。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the skin won't fully heal around it if you have any connector through the scalp.
zh: 如果你在头皮上有任何连接器,皮肤不会在它周围完全愈合。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're constantly at risk of a bacteria crawling down that into the brain and then the patient's gonna have a really bad time.
zh: 你时刻面临细菌顺着它爬进大脑的风险,那病人的日子会非常难熬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you really have to be able to close the skin.
zh: 所以你必须能够把皮肤完全闭合。

speaker: Unknown
en: That requires you to have implanted like a radio or transceiver of some sort and getting the power on that down, like there's a frontier at low power electronics, which is really important.
zh: 这就要求你植入某种无线电或收发器,并把它的功耗降下来——低功耗电子领域存在一条真正重要的前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: More, as I mentioned earlier, a lot of this is now becoming increasingly biology as our biological engineering capabilities increase.
zh: 还有,正如我之前提到的,随着我们生物工程能力的提升,其中越来越多的部分正在变成生物学问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then on those implants, ironically, one of the harder, more open problems is what we call packaging.
zh: 但讽刺的是,在这些植入体上,其中一个更难、更开放的问题是我们所谓的封装。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our colleagues in Europe call it tropicalization.
zh: 我们在欧洲的同行把它叫作 tropicalization。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is your ability to keep your device in and the body out of an implant that you put in the body.
zh: 这指的是你把设备放进身体后,让设备留在里面、把身体挡在外面的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are no truly passive surfaces anywhere in the body.
zh: 因为身体里没有任何真正惰性的表面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even bone is constantly getting remolded.
zh: 连骨骼都在不断地被重塑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if I put a device in, it's going to be, it's going to be getting attacked by the body and it's not regenerating itself.
zh: 所以如果我放进一个设备,它会一直被身体攻击,而它自己不会再生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need a material that is going to survive that for an extended period of time.
zh: 所以你需要一种能在很长时间内经受住这种情况的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: The very, like the classic example of this is the laser welded titanium can, which like, if you've seen like a pacemaker or deep brain stimulator, they've got this big titanium box.
zh: 最经典的例子就是激光焊接的钛壳，如果你见过心脏起搏器或脑深部刺激器的话，它们有一个很大的钛盒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously we can't put a big titanium box in the eye.
zh: 显然我们没法把一个大钛盒放进眼睛里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, one of the, the earlier retinal prostheses before
zh: 有趣的是，其中一个……更早期的视网膜假体在

speaker: Unknown
en: But for us, 10 years ago, was a device that did have a titanium box that they attached to the eyeball.
zh: 但对我们来说，10 年前，有一个设备确实有一个钛盒，他们把它固定在眼球上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a four-and-a-half-hour surgery.
zh: 那是一场四个半小时的手术。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had a little belt that went around the eyeball with a little titanium box on the side of the eye with a battery and a little PCB.
zh: 他们有一条绕在眼球上的小带子，在眼睛一侧装了一个小钛盒，里面有电池和一块小 PCB。

speaker: Unknown
en: This didn't work.
zh: 这没有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was not good enough.
zh: 这不够好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They needed to get rid of that somehow.
zh: 他们需要以某种方式摆脱那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our case, we've solved this with the laser projection trick where we power it wirelessly.
zh: 在我们的案例中，我们用激光投射的技巧解决了这个问题，我们通过无线方式供电。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having this next-generation packaging, some type of conformal coating that we can use to protect the implant that is not degraded by the body, is also not harmful to the body, and is resistant to all of the ways that the body will try and kill it, that material science is a very open-ended field.
zh: 拥有这种下一代封装，某种我们可以用来保护植入体的保形涂层，它不会被身体降解，也不会对身体有害，并且能抵抗身体试图杀死它的所有方式，这个材料科学是一个非常开放的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're interested in material science, that is a thing that we need progress in.
zh: 如果你对材料科学感兴趣，这正是我们需要取得进展的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you approach interacting with the medical field to build your retinal implant?
zh: 你是如何与医学领域打交道来建造你的视网膜植入体的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, business is just like a fancy word for talking to people and doing things.
zh: 我是说，生意其实就是一个用来形容「和人交谈并做事」的花哨词。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you talk to them, like you send them emails.
zh: 就是你和他们交谈，给他们发邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is the...
zh: 我是说，这就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So for our retinal implant, it was originally invented by a professor at Stanford almost 15 years ago, I think.
zh: 对于我们的视网膜植入体，它最初是由斯坦福的一位教授在大约 15 年前发明的，我记得。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was licensed to a European company that we were tracking.
zh: 它被授权给了一家我们一直在关注的欧洲公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me back up a second.
zh: 让我退回来说一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we started the company, I came from Neuralink, four of my five co-founders came from Neuralink.
zh: 当我们创办公司时，我来自 Neuralink，我的五位联合创始人中有四位来自 Neuralink。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of took a look around the world in early 2021 and asked, like, what is the most valuable thing that we can do that would be likely to work in the near future that would may have a big impact on patients and allow us to be the foundation for the type of scalable medical device company that we wanted to build?
zh: 我们在 2021 年初环顾了整个世界，问，什么是我们能做的最有价值的事情，它可能在不久的将来会成功，可能对患者产生重大影响，并能让我们成为我们想建造的那种可扩展的医疗设备公司的基础？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we came to the conclusion that restoring vision to the blind by stimulating the retina was the thing.
zh: 我们得出的结论是，通过刺激视网膜来让盲人重见光明就是那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that, you kind of have a choice of two types of cells in the retina that you can stimulate, these things called bipolar cells or the optic nerve.
zh: 在这方面，你可以选择刺激视网膜中的两类细胞，即所谓的双极细胞，或者视神经。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could do that electrically or you could do that optically.
zh: 你可以用电学的方式做，也可以用光学的方式做。

speaker: Unknown
en: We explored all four quadrants of that.
zh: 我们探索了这四个象限的全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: We developed internally a state-of-the-art gene therapy that optically stimulated one of those cells.
zh: 我们在内部开发了一种最先进的基因疗法，可以光学刺激其中一类细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we identified this French company as being the state-of-the-art in electrical stimulation.
zh: 而我们认定这家法国公司是电刺激领域最先进的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we, I mean, it's a small community.
zh: 所以我们，我是说，这是一个很小的圈子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can meet people, you can talk to them.
zh: 你可以认识人，可以和他们交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It eventually made sense for us to acquire them.
zh: 最终收购他们对我们来说是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ended up with the license, the technology, and we work with surgeons and doctors all the time.
zh: 我们最终获得了授权和技术，而且我们一直和外科医生以及医生合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if there's a new surgery that you want to figure out, I mean, typically this is best going through networks so that people are more likely to respond to your email.
zh: 比如如果你想搞清楚一种新手术，通常这最好通过人脉网络来进行，这样人们更可能回复你的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we cold email surgeons all the time saying like, hey, we have a weird surgery to develop.
zh: 但我们也经常冷邮件联系外科医生说，嘿，我们有一个奇怪的手术要开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to be a consultant?
zh: 你想当顾问吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And people reply.
zh: 而且人们会回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before I get to the next question, there is a real cultural thing here.
zh: 在我进入下一个问题之前，这里有一个真实的文化问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in my time hanging out around the periphery of SpaceX, I observed that like at least circa seven or eight years ago, probably like 20% of that company is what you might characterize as committed Martian colonists and 80% are serious engineers.
zh: 在我徘徊于 SpaceX 外围的那段时间里，我观察到，至少在大约七八年前，那家公司大概有 20% 的人可以被称为坚定的火星殖民者，80% 是严肃的工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that those people are lunatics and they just want to work on the highest performance Methalox engines in the world.
zh: 我认为那些人是疯子，他们只是想研究世界上性能最高的甲烷液氧发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need both of those cultures to be really successful long-term.
zh: 而要真正长期成功，你需要这两种文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's especially tricky in medicine, right?
zh: 这在医学领域尤其棘手，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's a very, very conservative, arguably very authoritarian culture for the most part.
zh: 因为那是一个非常、非常保守的，可以说在大多数情况下非常威权的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly at our company, we have, I'd say, 30%
zh: 同样，在我们的公司，我们，我要说，有 30%

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's an overtly transhumanist mission.
zh: 我是说，这是一个公开的超越人文主义/超人类主义的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then 70% like serious clinicians and scientists and researchers and people who think that those guys are crazy, but we're going to build some really valuable medical devices for critical unmet needs in the process.
zh: 然后另外 70% 是严肃的临床医生、科学家、研究人员，以及认为那些人是疯子、但认为我们会在这个过程中为关键的未满足需求建造一些真正有价值的医疗设备的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the things that makes
zh: 我认为，让

speaker: Unknown
en: Science, the company, very special is that it has both of those cultures and is able to integrate them.
zh: Science 这家公司非常特别的一件事是，它同时拥有这两种文化，并且能够将它们融合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're able to simultaneously do some really cool research that I think is really at the edge of the Overton window while simultaneously running clinical trials in six countries, now with an approved medical device in Europe and clinical trial results in the New England Journal of Medicine.
zh: 我们能够同时做一些我认为真正处于 Overton 窗口边缘的非常酷的研究，同时在六个国家开展临床试验，如今在欧洲拥有一个已获批的医疗设备，临床试验结果发表在《新英格兰医学杂志》上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to navigate both of those things, I think, to really reshape the future.
zh: 我认为，你必须能够驾驭这两者，才能真正重塑未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Has biotech gotten easier to break into for earlier stage founders?
zh: 对于早期创始人来说，生物科技是不是变得更容易进入了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Biotech remains capital intensive, and so that is... Like, I don't know that I'd recommend biotech if you have a choice of other stuff to do.
zh: 生物科技仍然是资本密集型的,所以这……如果可以选择做其他事情的话,我不确定我会推荐生物科技。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, for me, this was...
zh: 对我来说,我想这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I got, like...
zh: 我,呃……

speaker: Unknown
en: I realized almost 30 years ago that if you could engineer, like if you could alter the brain, you could alter reality.
zh: 大约 30 年前我就意识到,如果你能够改造工程,如果你能够改变大脑,你就能改变现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this was one of the biggest missions of the next 30, 40 years was building these things.
zh: 这是未来 30、40 年最大的使命之一,就是建造这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for me, I think it's like, every now and then, I think that my life would be way easier if I had just gone into AI instead of ECI.
zh: 所以对我而言,我想,时不时地,我会觉得如果我当时直接进了 AI 而不是 ECI,我的生活会轻松得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But somebody has to do it.
zh: 但总得有人来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's important to...
zh: 而且我认为重要的是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Biotech is hard.
zh: 生物科技很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a much harder path than many other things that you can do, but when you're successful, it has an impact on really what you see elsewhere.
zh: 它是一条比许多其他事情都艰难得多的路,但当你成功时,它的影响会真正体现在你在其他地方所看到的东西上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think increasingly there's...
zh: 我认为越来越多地有……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it was Paul Graham that wrote a long time ago that you get vibes in different cities and like the vibe in Cambridge, Massachusetts is you should be smarter or the vibe in New York is you should be wealthier.
zh: 我是说,Paul Graham 很久以前就写过,不同的城市有不同的氛围,比如马萨诸塞州剑桥的氛围是你应该更聪明,纽约的氛围是你应该更富有。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vibe in San Francisco is you should be more powerful, especially with the rise of things like artificial intelligence.
zh: 旧金山的氛围是你应该更有权势,尤其是在人工智能这类东西崛起之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people realize that this isn't just about money.
zh: 我认为人们意识到,这不只是关于钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of the most effective startup founders, it's not about the money.
zh: 在最有效的创业公司创始人那里,这不是关于钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about changing.
zh: 而是关于改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some way in which you want the world to be different.
zh: 你在某种方式上希望世界变得不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just turns out that for that project, the for-profit company is an incredibly powerful way to marshal the resources required to cause the world to be different in that way.
zh: 而事实证明,对于那个项目来说,营利性公司是调动所需资源、让世界以那种方式变得不同的一种极其有力的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is not about money.
zh: 这不是关于钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is about power.
zh: 这是关于力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are many different types of power.
zh: 而力量有很多不同的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's economic power.
zh: 有经济力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's military power.
zh: 有军事力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the power to heal the sick is a very dramatic one.
zh: 但治愈病人的力量是一种非常了不起的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you get that, not only is that
zh: 当你拥有它时,不仅仅是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that a real force to reshape the world?
zh: 这难道不是一种重塑世界的真实力量吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one that can be shared very readily.
zh: 而且它是一种可以非常容易地分享的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't share military power or economic power, but you can share the power of restoring sight to the blind or of giving life to the cancer patient.
zh: 你无法分享军事力量或经济力量,但你可以分享让盲人重见光明或让癌症病人重获生命的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the world is getting more complicated and there's big impacts of all the things that are being worked on by the people in this room.
zh: 我认为世界正变得越来越复杂,而在座各位所从事的工作都在产生巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And biotech is hard.
zh: 生物科技很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very capital intensive.
zh: 它非常资本密集。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a long road.
zh: 它是一条漫长的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you start a company in this space, you're committing to a decade of your life that you will never get back, no matter how it turns out.
zh: 当你在这一领域创办公司时,你是在承诺投入你人生中的十年,无论结果如何,这十年都不会再回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The results of that when it works, the impact that this has on patients and their families is really unlike really any other sector.
zh: 而当它成功时,其结果给病人及其家属带来的影响,真的不同于任何其他行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the last question, what's a popular belief in tech that you think is wrong?
zh: 那么最后一个问题,你认为科技界有什么流行观点是错的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't even know what the popular beliefs in tech are now.
zh: 我甚至不知道现在科技界的流行观点是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I mean, okay, even the whole basis of building Elix is contrarian.
zh: 嗯,我是说,好吧,连创办 Elix 的整个基础都是反共识的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I think that if you raise a Series A and then you tell your investors that you're going to vibe code a purchasing system, I think that any reasonable board is going to, like, ask you what you're thinking.
zh: 比如,我认为如果你融了一轮 Series A,然后告诉你的投资人你要用 vibe coding 写一个采购系统,我认为任何理智的董事会都会问你到底在想什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, we were able to do that because I never got those questions because we don't, because I control the company.
zh: 而我们能够做到这一点,是因为我从来没有收到过那些质问,因为我们不,因为我控制着这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's one narrow example, I guess.
zh: 不过,我想,这只是个狭隘的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
